verdicts.reasoning:
The observation reproduces: every number checks out and the band is there at full size. What I could not confirm is that it is a fault. Four reasons.

1. The sheen is unchanged and physical. It is the same as in round 3 (G ratio 0.89-1.04; outline 0.129-0.137), slightly lower than round 4 after the softbox fix. It is within textbook Fresnel for acrylic reflecting the studio's side walls. On the key side it is lighter than the face; on the shadow side it is at the face's lightness, and it keeps the face's hue. That is a sheen following the light, not a coat.

2. The red under it is the correct second pass. It fell by about the same factor across the whole width (0.40-0.48 / 0.50-0.65). The same sheen over half the red has to take more of the outline, so the wider band is arithmetic, not a new error. The lane's even-light dome test already found satin body shares of only 0.25-0.41 at 55-65 deg even with one tinted pass. It also traced the extra fall-off at the foot corners to the floor and the contact shadow. I did not re-run that part myself.

3. The finding's target cannot be reached honestly. Round 4's C* of 17-30 at the flanks was the single-pass value. Keeping it at round 5's depth would mean cutting the sheen below Fresnel or adding red at the edges. Either would misstate the satin, which is the owner's worst case.

4. It is not round 3 coming back. The gray core is about half as wide. Measured against each round's own face, the band is 65-75 % of round 3's width. Round 3's band was darker than the face and neutral gray.

The critic and I agree that at 480 and in the 300 px row it reads as shading.

Severity: note. If the owner wants redder edges at full zoom, the physical lever is the studio: dark flags beside the base, out of frame. That would also darken the ball's rim reflections, so it is a lighting choice, not a material fix.

(3) I fitted each rim pixel (4-40 px in, rows 1520-1700) as a non-negative linear-light mix of the base's own body (90-110 px in) and the ground 6-14 px outside the outline. r5 fits body plus the cream ground at dE median 0.30 left and 0.26 right; the same fit with neutral gray gives 1.83 and 1.39. r3 is the reverse: body plus neutral gray fits at 0.19 and 0.76, body plus cream at 2.63 and 2.09. r4's rim was also a neutral-gray sheen (0.23 and 0.38).
(4) Sheen strength, measured as (rim G minus body G) over ground G on the left flank, is the same in r5 and r4 to within 0.02 at every depth and row: 4 px 0.16-0.29, 20 px 0.16-0.19, 50 px 0.07-0.09. This follows smooth acrylic Fresnel (n 1.49) at 20-50 px (F 0.08-0.19) and sits below it at the rim (F 0.28-0.45). The rim's linear G is not higher in r5 (left rim 4 px: 189-206 in r5, 219-232 in r4). On the lit left flank, r5's body red holds out to the rim (linear R 243-290 at the rim against 296 at 200 px in); r3's collapsed (158-246 against 470-624).
(5) Compared on patches with no highlights, the r5 base front middle is 32.4/61.6/h36 and the left-middle 31.9/54.2/h34, against the ball's lower body 40.9/64.8/h34 and left body 42.9/56.7/h31. The base is 6-9 L* darker, but only 2.5-3 C* lower and the same hue; it is not 15 C* duller. r4 matched the ball only as a median. Its base front was 61.7/59.4/h25 (upper) and 46.8/72.1/h31 (middle): 6-21 L* lighter and pinker, which is the one-pass bug.

Looking at my own crops: at 3x, r5's left flank and foot corner show a warm taupe rim about 20-30 px wide (full size), and r3 shows a slate band over 40 px wide with gray-black blotches. At 960, r5 has only a faint soft edge. At 480 x 600 and in the 300 px row (next to the Tropos, pendant and Mantle), I see no film; the base reads as deep satin wine-red. r3's patches are visible at 300.
verdicts.reasoning:
The numbers reproduce, but the claim that r5 goes "halfway back toward round 3" does not hold, and the finding fails on three of the refutation grounds.

First, the physics is right. The flank sheen in r5 has the same strength as in r4, the round the critic wants to return to, and its strength matches what an acrylic surface must reflect at those viewing angles. The only changes are underneath and in color. The body red under the sheen is deeper because of the two-pass tint fix, so the same sheen looks paler against it; that fully explains why the outline stayed at L* 41-55 while the centre darkened. And the sheen is now the cream of the studio the lamp actually stands in, where r3 and r4 had a neutral-gray sheen. That also inverts the critic's guess about the walls: the walls now visible in r5 made the rim warm, not gray.

Second, it is not the same thing as r3. r3's "smoke" was a neutral gray film, with the red body dropping out at the flanks. r5 has neither.

Third, it is invisible at the sizes that matter. Nothing shows at 480 or in the 300 px row.

Two parts of the evidence are misread. The L*<20 share is the saturated foot band, not smoke. The "9 L* darker, 15 C* duller than the ball" figure compares whole-mask medians: the ball's includes its highlights, and the base's includes its rims and foot band. Like-for-like, the base is the same hue, 2.5-3 C* lower and 6-9 L* darker. The darker value is what the optical-contact tint and the ball's overhang should give, and it fits the owner's "deep color" rule. The critic's target, "median within 3 L* of the ball, flanks C* 30 or more within 40 px", relies on r4's buggy one-pass base. Even r4 did not meet it: its outer 3-20 px were C* 20-29. It cannot be met without lightening the body, which would undo the deeper color.

What remains is a note. At full size the left flank shows a warm satin sheen, and the owner asked about exactly this edge. If the lane answers him, it should show him a full-size crop and explain that this is the satin catching the sweep, not relight the base.
